established_findings.statement: Large language models can be used to translate high-level network intents into low-level network/NFV configurations with encouraging accuracy in published prototypes and experiments.
limitations: Evaluations are primarily prototype-scale or limited-scope experiments (NFV or specific IBN cases).
Vendor/device diversity and large production topologies are not comprehensively evaluated in these records.

established_findings.statement: Augmenting LLMs with external tools (APIs, specialized toolkits, retrieval, or domain analyzers) improves task grounding, correctness, and capability for complex domain workflows in multiple published systems.
limitations: Most demonstrations are in non-NetOps domains (chemistry, drilling, multi-API benchmarks) or general tool-agent runtimes; direct NetOps impact is implied but not fully measured end-to-end in production networks.

established_findings.statement: Generate–validate–repair (localize–fix–validate) is a recommended architectural approach for automated configuration repair, drawing on analogies to automated program repair and explicit proposals for network configuration repair.
limitations: Proposals and analogies exist; few large-scale NetOps deployments demonstrating end-to-end automated repair under realistic operational constraints are reported in the supplied records.

established_findings.statement: LLMs exhibit hallucinations and unreliable outputs; entropy/verification-based uncertainty estimators and retrieval/verification augmentation can detect or reduce such failures.
limitations: Techniques reduce but do not eliminate hallucinations; calibration and cross-judge agreement remain challenges per supplied clinical-evaluation analogues.

established_findings.statement: Agent/tool/runtime configuration can materially change safety and correctness outcomes of tool-using LLM agents (configuration-level semantic brittleness documented experimentally).
limitations: Findings are from structured red-teaming experiments across multiple models; transfer to specific NetOps deployments needs domain-specific evaluation.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent do LLM-based intent→configuration translators generalize across vendor-specific CLIs, diverse protocols, and large production topologies without vendor-specific tailoring?
limitations: Records demonstrate feasibility on selected cases but do not provide comprehensive cross-vendor, cross-protocol generalization data.

unresolved_questions.statement: How effectively and at what operational cost can deterministic network verifiers and simulators be integrated into closed-loop LLM toolchains at production scale to prevent unsafe configuration commits?
limitations: Surveys and proposals suggest integration; supplied records lack large-scale production measurements of verifier-augmented LLM loops in NetOps.

unresolved_questions.statement: What is the quantitative effect of tool-augmentation (RAG, specialized APIs, verification tools) on reducing real-world NetOps misconfiguration and incident rates?
limitations: Empirical evidence of operational incident-rate reduction is not present in the supplied NetOps-specific records; most measured gains are in other domains or at prototype scale.

candidate_gaps.statement: Absence of a standardized, public benchmark and dataset suite for LLM-based network-intent translation, configuration synthesis, and automated configuration repair that pairs realistic topologies, vendor CLIs, and deterministic validators.
limitations: Supplied records include domain benchmarks and benchmark-building examples in other areas (API-Bank, RAG surveys) and proposals for ACR but do not show a NetOps LLM benchmark; absence is inferred from the provided corpus rather than an exhaustive external search.

candidate_gaps.statement: Need for verification-based confidence estimators tailored to LLM-generated network configurations (combining symbolic/verifier checks with LLM-derived uncertainty signals).
limitations: Verification-based confidence methods are demonstrated in clinical and general LLM settings; specific designs for network-config outputs remain to be developed and validated.

candidate_gaps.statement: Systematic adversarial/robustness evaluation targeted at LLM-generated network configurations (attacks that lead to unsafe network behavior) is underexplored in the supplied records.
limitations: Adversarial ML surveys exist; concrete NetOps-targeted adversarial datasets and evaluations are not present among the supplied records.

excluded_claims: LLMs are already production-ready to autonomously operate and fully manage real-world NetOps without human oversight (unsupported by supplied records).
Tool-augmenting an LLM guarantees zero misconfigurations or eliminates the need for deterministic verification (no supplied record demonstrates elimination of all failures).
There exists a public, standardized NetOps LLM benchmark encompassing vendor CLIs, topologies, and validators (no such benchmark is present in the supplied records).
Any single LLM family or model consistently outperforms others across all NetOps tasks and safety metrics (supplied records do not support such a universal superiority claim).

The supplied corpus contains a deployed, large-scale field study showing incident-rate reduction from LLM-driven automated configuration in production networks (no such field study is in the provided records).
